name: Calm
tagline: Calm faces the hardest behavioral design challenge in consumer tech: building habits for an activity users genuinely want to quit doing early.
key_insight: Calm's behavioral design challenge is philosophically interesting: can you ethically use behavioral science to help people build habits that may eliminate the need for your product? Calm's answer is content expansion — become a 'wellness platform' rather than a 'meditation app.' But this risks cognitive load creep as the product tries to be everything at once.
top_evidence: Sleep Stories drove 2x more DAU than meditation (Bloomberg 2023). McConaughey's Sleep Story played 100M+ times. 10-min default maximized D7 retention (WWDC 2022).

techniques.title: Gentle Default Nudges
techniques.description: Calm defaults new users to a 10-minute 'Daily Calm' session — long enough to feel meaningful, short enough to not intimidate. The daily reminder is positioned as an invitation, not a demand. This gentle default architecture contrasts sharply with Duolingo's loss-aversion-driven approach.
techniques.evidence: Calm's user research (WWDC 2022 case study): 10-minute default was A/B tested against 5, 15, and 20 minutes. 10 minutes maximized D7 retention while maintaining perceived session value.

techniques.title: The Wellness App Retention Paradox
techniques.description: Meditation apps face a unique challenge: users who succeed at building a meditation practice may not need the app anymore. Calm addresses this by continuously expanding content (Sleep Stories, music, nature sounds) to serve adjacent needs. But the core tension remains — if the app fulfills its promise (you feel calm), the motivation to open it decreases.
techniques.evidence: Calm's D90 retention (~8%) is industry-typical for wellness apps but far below social/entertainment apps (~25%). This isn't a design failure — it may reflect genuine user success.

techniques.title: Sleep Stories as Habit Stacking
techniques.description: Sleep Stories (narrated bedtime stories for adults) stack onto an existing habit (going to bed). This is the most effective trigger in Hook Model design — not a push notification, but a natural context that already occurs daily. By anchoring to bedtime, Calm gets a 'free' daily trigger without any notification infrastructure.
techniques.evidence: Calm CEO reported Sleep Stories drove 2x more daily active users than meditation content (Bloomberg, 2023). Matthew McConaughey's Sleep Story has been played 100M+ times.

strengths: Content quality creates genuine user value
weaknesses: Annual subscription creates pressure to justify cost
